text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Romania needs to import some 200,000 tonnes of wheat to cover domestic demand until July, the paper says.
- Shortage of funds to purchase fodder have serioulsy affected the state-run animal farms, the paper says.
- Romania's National Development Agency plans package of measures to boost foreign investments in the country.
- The Defence Ministry's 1997 budget will amount to 2.85 percent of the GDP, the paper says.

- The Brasov-based Intreprinderea Aeronautica Romana helicopter maker hopes to sign contract with Bell Helicopter Textron of the United States to co-produce 96 Cobra attack helicopters, the paper says.
- Embassies and consulates in Romania have the right to purchase land in Romania to build their headquarters.
- The prime ministers of Romania and Hungary will cooperate for early admission to NATO, the paper says.

- Romanian Foreign Minister Adrian Severin will meet U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright during an official visit to Washington on April 21. The paper also says President Emil Constantinescu might visit the U.S. in "the near future".

- One case of typhoid fever was reported in Romania's south-eastern city of Braila. Doctors said the desease was caused by the polluted water coming from the Danube river. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
